references.text: Describes the places of refuge for someone who kills another by accident, without intent. This is the foundational text about cities of refuge.
Elaborates on the criteria for unintentional killing, where the person was not an enemy and had no malicious intent, corresponding to 'without knowing it' and 'had not hated him beforehand'.
Early legislation regarding unintentional killing in which God designates a place of flight, a precursor to the city-of-refuge system.
Joshua's implementation of the cities of refuge, using the same language about unintentional killing and the absence of prior enmity.
Summarizes the purpose of the cities of refuge for someone who kills a person without intent.
Uses the same expressions 'without knowing it' and 'had not hated him beforehand' to describe the conditions for seeking refuge.
The Epistle to the Hebrews uses the city-of-refuge concept as an image of the hope we have in Christ, where believers 'flee to lay hold of the hope set before us'.
